answer.note: All four ref files hold the same generic text and give no file-specific priority, so I chose the refs from the code. C (dogwhistle/visibility.py) is the best match. It defines ARMS = ("codeword","public","explicit"), the only three-arm set in the package. It also has receive() at line 141. A (dogwhistle/study.py) is second. Its receive() at line 251 checks the sender seal digest, and it has public_ledger_digest_path and the ledger-writing code. I did not read the receive() bodies, so I haven't confirmed that visibility.py resumes a verified ordered checkpoint or writes a private receiver ledger plus a public digest. honest.py and listener.py have only two arms, and heldout.py has no arm set. Suggested 60-minute split: visibility.py 30 min, study.py 15 min (the shared digest and checkpoint helpers), honest.py 10 min, heldout.py 5 min. Confirm the checkpoint-resume and ledger-digest behaviour in visibility.py first.
